## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

T829 in one fascicle is the Táng re-translation of the *Anakṣara-karaṇḍaka-vairocana-garbha-sūtra*, parallel to *[Wúzì bǎoqiè jīng 無字寶篋經 (T828)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0534)* by Bodhiruci of the Northern Wèi. Translated by the central-Indian Táng translator [地婆訶羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%B0%E5%A9%86%E8%A8%B6%E7%BE%85) (Divākara, 614–688) at Cháng'ān during his Yífèng 儀鳳 to Chuígǒng 垂拱 (676–688) translation career under Empress Wǔ Zétiān's patronage. The Táng title 大乘離文字普光明藏 ("Mahāyāna [Sūtra of the] Universally-Radiant Treasury Free of Letters") more transparently reflects the Sanskrit *vairocana-garbha* component (普光明藏 *pǔguāngmíng zàng* = *vairocana-garbha*).

**Abstract**

The narrative frame and doctrinal content are identical to those of [T828](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0534): at Mt Gṛdhrakūṭa near Rājagṛha, the Buddha is surrounded by countless bodhisattvas, all "skilful in penetrating the letterless *dharma*-gate," all "freed from the three realms." The bodhisattva-list partially parallels T828, with some name-equivalents adjusted to Divākara's translation register: **Shèngsīwéi** 勝思惟 (= T828's same name), **Fǎzhènyīn** 法震音 (= T828's 法響), **Miàoshēn** 妙身, **Fǎwǎng** 法輞, etc. The bodhisattva Shèngsīwéi asks the same two questions: what is the one *dharma* the *bodhisattva* extinguishes, and what is the one *dharma* the Tathāgata awakens to. The Buddha's exposition follows the same arc — extinguishing greed, hatred, delusion, self-view, laziness, sleep, craving, ignorance — and culminates in the doctrine of the *anakṣara-dharma*-ground.

Divākara's translation idiom is more polished than Bodhiruci's earlier effort, deploying the standard late-seventh-century Buddhist Chinese technical vocabulary (e.g. 普光明藏 for *vairocana-garbha*, 離文字 for *anakṣara*). The doctrinal content is unchanged. See [KR6i0534](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0534) for the full doctrinal summary.
